task_instance: Run the default small-warehouse Nova Carter Mission Control showcase in --preflight mode (read-only checks: local Isaac Sim installation with GUI, Docker cloud stack, NVIDIA GPU/driver, display) as described in the SKILL.md Default workflow step 2.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable requires launching a locally installed Isaac Sim in a GUI window on the host display, backed by an NVIDIA GPU with driver R590+ and a 64GB-class host, plus a running Docker daemon for the Mission Control cloud stack and Nova Carter SIL container. This sandbox has none of these: `nvidia-smi` is not found (no NVIDIA GPU/driver present), there is no X display (DISPLAY is unset, only Xvfb headless available, not a real host GUI window), no Isaac Sim installation exists anywhere on the machine, and the Docker daemon is not running (`docker ps` fails to connect to the socket) even though the docker CLI binary is present. None of these are things that can be worked around with the file/shell/browser abilities this runtime grants — GPU-accelerated 3D rendering hardware and a live GUI display are physical/runtime capabilities absent from this container, not merely uninstalled software. Per the skill's own rules, if nothing is installed it must route to isaac-sim-installation rather than proceeding, and that installation itself needs a real GPU/driver stack this runtime cannot provide.
evidence: Ran from work dir: `which nvidia-smi` -> not found; `nvidia-smi` -> command not found (no GPU/driver). `which docker` -> /usr/bin/docker present but `docker ps` -> 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?' (daemon not available). `echo $DISPLAY` -> empty (no host GUI display); only Xvfb (headless X) present, not a real display Isaac Sim's GUI window could render into. `ls ~/isaacsim` -> No such file or directory; `find / -iname isaac-sim*` -> no results (no Isaac Sim installation on the machine, and none could be feasibly installed/licensed/downloaded here). Given the skill explicitly forbids proceeding without a compatible GPU-backed local Isaac Sim install and a live display, and requires Docker for the cloud stack/Nova Carter SIL, the showcase's core deliverable (watching Carter navigate a route in a live Isaac Sim GUI window with Mission Control reporting COMPLETED) cannot be attempted, let alone verified, in this runtime.
